- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first 10–15 days, followed by a sharp downward correction — suggesting model fails to capture sudden market corrections or policy-driven price drops.
- After a spike in true values (e.g., 79.14, 80.24), model forecasts overshoot and remain elevated for several days, failing to adjust to subsequent declines.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: it tends to forecast a flat or slightly increasing trend even when true values show strong volatility or sharp reversals.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt drops or spikes in true values, especially in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show a downward trend or sharp correction.
- Model fails to adjust for recent volatility — if true values show a sharp drop, forecast remains unchanged or only slightly adjusted.
- Model overestimates the “recovery” phase after a drop — tends to forecast a gradual recovery instead of a sharp rebound or correction.
- Forecasts are not sensitive to recent price spikes — model ignores recent high values and continues to forecast a flat or slightly increasing trend.
- Model exhibits a lag in adjusting to true values — often takes 3–5 days to correct after a sharp drop or spike.
